scores.claim_text: Raytheon segment is the prime contractor on the Long Range Stand Off Weapon (LRSO), explicitly named as one of Raytheon's air-to-air/air-to-ground weapons portfolio anchors.
scores.interpretation: LRSO (AGM-181) is the air-launched nuclear cruise missile replacing AGM-86B; per public DoD nuclear modernization plans it sits inside Air Force RDT&E (likely PE 0101127F or successor) and is largely classified. Our 410-PE J-Book corpus does not cover it. Per heuristic #7, NOT_FOUND for a major classified strategic program is a COVERAGE GAP, not a red flag. Treat as UNVERIFIABLE; do not penalize.

scores.claim_text: Pratt & Whitney is sole-source producer of the F135 engine for the F-35 Joint Program Office. In 2023 Pratt & Whitney booked $2.5 billion for F135 production plus $2.2 billion for F135 sustainment, making F135 the largest single program backlog booking in the segment.
scores.M_value: F-35 C2D2 FUNDED_STEADY ($1.237B FY24); F-35 Squadrons FUNDED_STEADY ($89M FY24); F135 itself NOT_FOUND (procurement line not in our corpus)
scores.interpretation: F-35 ecosystem RDT&E is fully funded at the cutoff. The F135 is the sole-source engine; absence of a TERMINATE/UNFUNDED signal across multiple F-35 PEs supports the claim that F135 backlog is real. USAspending DoD contracts for 'Pratt & Whitney' returned only 36 awards / $19.8M — substring noise (Pratt & Whitney Engine Services is the typical recipient name and FMS goes via Joint Program Office), not a verification miss. Backlog claim is consistent with the J-Book at the cutoff.

scores.claim_text: Pratt & Whitney is in the prototype phase of the Next Generation Adaptive Propulsion (NGAP) program for the U.S. Air Force, having booked $232 million in 2023 for the prototype phase — forward-looking exposure to NGAP-driven sixth-gen fighter propulsion.
scores.M_value: FUNDED_STEADY at $573.8M FY24 (latest visible year at cutoff)
scores.interpretation: NGAP prototype phase is funded at the cutoff at substantial scale. Pratt's $232M booking is consistent with being one of two NGAP prototype primes (the other typically GE Aerospace). PASS at the cutoff. NOTE for future cutoff updates: the FY26 J-Book shows NGAP DECLINING from $574M to $507M (FY25) to $330M (FY26) as NGAD propulsion competition narrows — a forward concern post-cutoff but not visible to the framework at 2024-09-01 with cutoff filter applied.

scores.claim_text: Raytheon's strategic missile defense growth in 2023 was driven by the Next Generation Interceptor (NGI) program, an MDA program where Raytheon competes (as a Northrop Grumman team partner) against the Lockheed Martin team for the homeland missile defense interceptor.
scores.M_check: pentagon_jbook.query_program_funding(pe_number="0604874C" Improved Homeland Defense Interceptors) + (program_name="Next Generation Interceptor")
scores.M_value: NGI by name NOT_FOUND; Improved Homeland Defense Interceptors (the MDA PE that funds NGI development) FUNDED_STEADY at $2.074B FY24
scores.interpretation: PE 0604874C (Improved Homeland Defense Interceptors) is the MDA RDT&E line that funds NGI; at the cutoff it is well-funded at over $2B/year. The claim that NGI drove Raytheon strategic-missile-defense growth is consistent with strong, growing MDA RDT&E. Note: Raytheon's NGI team partnership (with Northrop Grumman) competes against the Lockheed Martin team — the MDA was expected to down-select in FY25. The claim is a competitive-pipeline claim, not a booked-revenue claim; J-Book status supports the addressable opportunity.

scores.claim_text: Raytheon booked $1.2 billion to provide Patriot Air Defense systems to Switzerland in 2023 and 'proven Patriot air and missile defense system' is named as a core layered air defense product line. Patriot pipeline (FMS + LTAMDS upgrade path) is a key forward driver.
scores.M_check: pentagon_jbook.query_program_funding for Patriot, LTAMDS, Lower Tier Air and Missile Defense Sensor
scores.interpretation: Patriot, LTAMDS, NASAMS, Javelin, Stinger, Excalibur are all U.S. Army procurement/RDT&E programs. The 410-PE corpus does not appear to cover Army procurement (P-40) line items. Heuristic #7 applies: this is a coverage gap, not evidence against the claim. Patriot/LTAMDS demand at the cutoff was demonstrably strong from public DoD record (Switzerland FMS, Ukraine surge replenishment). UNVERIFIABLE — recommend extending corpus with Army Missiles & Space and Army Aircraft Procurement P-40s.

scores.claim_text: Pratt & Whitney's PW1100G-JM Geared Turbofan (GTF) commercial engine fleet is subject to the 'Powder Metal Matter' — a rare-condition in powder metal forcing accelerated inspection of the PW1100 GTF fleet, the largest disclosed risk in the filing and a multi-billion-dollar accrued liability impacting forward FCF.
scores.M_check: (no M-source query needed — claim is self-disclosure of a contingent liability)
scores.M_value: Disclosed as principal risk factor with multi-billion-dollar accrued liability; matches segment reorganization and customer-compensation accounting in the filing footnotes
scores.interpretation: This is a control / non-J-Book claim. RTX itself made the disclosure; the framework does not need external verification beyond confirming the company has filed updates (8-K). No edits to severity. PASS as a faithful self-disclosure; the magnitude (>$5B P&L charge in 2023) is the dominant near-term cash drag and is appropriately flagged in the filing.

scores.claim_text: Raytheon booked $2.8 billion in 2023 on a NATO Support and Procurement Agency (NSPA) contract for Guidance Enhanced Missiles (GEM-T) — Patriot interceptor variant for European demand.
scores.interpretation: GEM-T is a NATO/NSPA international procurement of Patriot PAC-2 GEM-T interceptors; it is NOT a U.S. Pentagon J-Book line item, it is a NATO buy. The J-Book corpus by design does not cover NATO procurement. UNVERIFIABLE per heuristic #7. The $2.8B booking is an FMS/NATO contract — verifiable via the State Department DSCA notification record, not pentagon_jbook.

scores.claim_text: Raytheon booked $7.8 billion in 2023 on 'a number of classified contracts', representing the single largest 2023 booking category — disclosed but undescribed black-budget exposure.
scores.M_value: 11,713 DoD awards totaling $70.9B over the window — consistent with the $7.8B classified plus disclosed unclassified bookings
scores.interpretation: Aggregate DoD obligations to Raytheon ($70.9B over 20 months) substantially exceed the disclosed segment-level booking figures, supporting the claim that disclosed classified bookings ($7.8B) are part of a much larger real DoD contract footprint. No claim inflation. PASS.
